subject: ClearStream: inference readiness, throughput targets, and multi-variant routing
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alexis Moreau <alexis@clearstream.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: ClearStream: inference readiness, throughput targets, and multi-variant routing

Alexis — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

Summary of what we heard
- Primary pain: production latency spikes under concurrent traffic (observed 95th percentile up to ~650ms for 256-token responses).
- Goal: consistent P95 latency <= 200ms for 256-token chats and sustained throughput of ~80 requests/sec during peak windows.
- Model: ClearStream plans to use an open LLM family (you referenced Llama-2-70B / a fine-tuned variant).
- Data concerns: need VPC private deployment for regulated PII flows and SOC 2 evidence for audit.
- Ops: want deterministic failover (multi-variant routing) — primary low-latency instance + cheaper fallback for degraded capacity.

Technical constraints and clarifying assumptions
- Target token length distribution: median 48, 95th 256 (you confirmed).
- Average prompt size: ~750 tokens total (includes system + user).
- KV-cache usage: likely helpful given repeated prefixes per user session.
- Quantization: you'd consider int8 if quality holds; we should validate with eval prompts.

Immediate asks from Redwood to unblock sizing and topology recommendation
1) Sample telemetry (1-2 hours) of production requests (timestamps, payload sizes, and p95 latencies) — pseudo-anonymized is fine.
2) Representative prompt set (you said you can share 50–100 prompts) — helps calibrate KV-cache hit rates and batch sizing.
3) Confirm whether model weights are the public Llama-2-70B or a private fork (license/weights impacts deployment options).
4) Procurement lead contact and timeline (if you can share a simple PDF with PO process it speeds Priv/Dedicated onboarding).

Proposed topology options (we'll size once we get telemetry + prompts)
A) Dedicated low-latency pool (preferred): 3x gpus with continuous batching + KV cache in front, pinned model, can meet P95 <= 200ms at target throughput with conservative kernel selection.
B) Private VPC deployment: mirrors Dedicated but hosted inside your VPC; needs onboarding window for network/argo config.
C) Hybrid multi-variant routing: route requests to primary pool; on SLO breach route 20% to cheaper quantized variants until primary recovers.

Next steps / timeline
- You: share telemetry + prompt set + procurement PDF (by EOW if possible).
- Redwood: I'll deliver a rough topology and cost range within 48 business hours of receiving artifacts.
- Schedule: propose a follow-up technical deep-dive with Markus and Grace next Tue 06/08 at 10am PT.

Attachments: call-recording-20270601.mp3 (recording), sample-prompt-set.csv (placeholder you agreed to send on the call).

If any item above is off, call it out. Otherwise I'll mark these action items and schedule the follow-up.

— Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Alexis Moreau <alexis@clearstream.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lin <jordan.lin@clearstream.ai>, procurement@clearstream.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearStream: inference readiness, throughput targets, and multi-variant routing

Thanks Jonas — this is great, and aligned with our notes. Quick confirmations and a couple of asks from our side: 

Confirmations
- We can provide the telemetry (redacted) and a 75-prompt sample by Friday EOD.
- Model: we are running a fine-tuned Llama-2-70B variant; weights are not gated but the fine-tune artifacts are internal.
- Primary requirement: P95 <= 200ms for 256 tokens as you wrote.

Asks
1) Can you include a short paragraph on quality regressions when switching to int8/quantized fallbacks (what test pass rate we should expect)?
2) Procurement: attached is a short PDF that outlines our legal review timeline and PO window — we generally need 4 weeks for standard SaaS buys.

We'd like the follow-up deep-dive to include a short demo of telemetry/observability in the Redwood Console (traces + token-level cost) so our infra team sees the ops flow. Jordan will coordinate scheduling.

Thanks — Alexis
VP, Platform Engineering | ClearStream AI
alexis@clearstream.ai | +33 6 12 34 56 78

Also request Alexis share a contact for their SRE who will be in the deep-dive.

Subject: Re: ClearStream: inference readiness, throughput targets, and multi-variant routing

Thanks all — noted and committing to the action items below. Forwarding our timeline and a couple of links for prep.

Action items (Redwood)
- Deliver initial topology + estimated monthly cost range (low/high) within 48 business hours after we get telemetry + prompts.
- Provide quantization quality summary (expected pass rates and recommended eval checklist) — Markus to own.
- Prep a short Redwood Console demo focused on traces and token cost for the deep-dive.

Action items (ClearStream)
- Send redacted telemetry and sample prompts (target: Fri 06/04 EOD).
- Share SRE contact for the deeper technical session.
- Procurement team: we got the PDF, thanks — Redwood sales will follow the PO process once topology is confirmed.

Proposed follow-up: Tue 2027-06-08 10:00am PT (60m) — I created a tentative HubSpot event (link below). If that works for everyone, Jordan please accept and add the SRE.

Links
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/CLSTR-2027-058
- Shared prep doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-clearstream-sandbox

If no objections, we'll treat Alexis's timelines as the gating path and I'll book Markus for the deep-dive.

— Jonas
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
